sentences.en: Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night.
sentences.zh: 研究者把电极贴在睡眠者的头上进行研究，结果发现，我们睡觉时有两种睡眠状态，整夜交替出现。

sentences.en: The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep.
sentences.zh: 第一种是快速眼动（REM）睡眠，也叫活动性睡眠。

sentences.en: During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，我们的眼睑虽然闭着，眼球却在转动。

sentences.en: Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves.
sentences.zh: 肌肉也会微微抽动，不过大部分肌肉都处于麻痹状态，因此我们不会伤到自己。

sentences.en: In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all.
sentences.zh: 与此相对，我们还会进入非快速眼动睡眠，在这一阶段身体几乎一动不动。

sentences.en: Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 大多数做梦的时候，人都处在快速眼动睡眠中；梦境最鲜明的时候尤其可以肯定是这样。

sentences.en: There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream.
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，其他哺乳动物可能也会做梦。

sentences.en: For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 例如，研究者把大鼠清醒时穿过迷宫的脑活动模式，同它们在快速眼动睡眠中的脑活动模式作了比较。

sentences.en: They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这两种模式极其相似，于是得出结论，睡着的大鼠梦见了自己穿过迷宫。

sentences.en: But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，在哺乳动物以外的动物身上寻找它们会做梦的证据更为困难。

sentences.en: Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping.
sentences.zh: 这些动物的大脑与人脑有很大差别，而且往往很难在它们睡觉时记录大脑的活动。

sentences.en: Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons.
sentences.zh: 不过，最近研究者成功记录到了鸽子睡着时的脑活动。

sentences.en: As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 与哺乳动物一样，这些记录显示鸽子也有快速眼动睡眠和非快速眼动睡眠。

sentences.en: Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.
sentences.zh: 耐人寻味的是，在快速眼动睡眠期间，负责处理视觉信息的脑区活动十分活跃，处理飞行等身体活动相关图像的脑区尤其如此。这提示，鸽子梦见的可能正是这类活动。

sentences.en: That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，做梦和快速眼动睡眠恐怕并非动物界所有动物共有的现象。

sentences.en: For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming.
sentences.zh: 例如，海绵没有大脑，也就缺乏做梦所需的生理结构。

sentences.en: There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns.
sentences.zh: 还有一些动物的睡眠方式与众不同。

sentences.en: These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake.
sentences.zh: 其中就有鲸和海豚。它们入睡时并不让整个大脑休息，只有一半进入休息状态，另一半保持清醒。

sentences.en: They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid.
sentences.zh: 它们也没有表现出快速眼动睡眠的迹象，这意味着它们可能只会在非快速眼动睡眠中做梦，而这种梦没有那么鲜明。

sentences.en: This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives.
sentences.zh: 这令人意外，因为我们往往认为，鲸和海豚的内心世界很复杂。

sentences.en: It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.
sentences.zh: 一种看法是，它们之所以不经历快速眼动睡眠，是因为动物在这一睡眠阶段更容易受到极端温度的伤害。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, in many cases REM sleep does seem to have benefits.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在许多情况下，快速眼动睡眠似乎确实有益。

sentences.en: Growing evidence from birds and mammals suggests that REM sleep and dreaming are important for forming memories and learning.
sentences.zh: 来自鸟类和哺乳动物的证据越来越多，表明快速眼动睡眠和做梦对记忆形成及学习都很重要。

sentences.en: It is believed that when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，经历过的事在梦中重现，有助于把记忆整合起来，转入更长期的储存。

sentences.en: As soon as animals evolved moderately complex lifestyles, they would have needed to dream in order to manage these lifestyles.
sentences.zh: 动物一旦演化出具有一定复杂程度的生活方式，想要应付这种生活，想必就需要做梦了。

sentences.en: However, we still don't understand how this outward behaviour relates to internal experience.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们依然不清楚，这种外在行为和动物内心的体验究竟有怎样的联系。

sentences.en: It seems impossible to know what it is like to be a rat or a pigeon, let alone imagine their dreamscapes.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎无法知道当一只大鼠或一只鸽子是什么感觉，更不用说想象它们的梦境了。

sentences.en: We are quick to interpret the twitching limbs and quiet barks of sleeping dogs, but the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits that comes along with that.
sentences.zh: 看着狗睡着时四肢抽动、听着它发出低低的叫声，我们很快就会给这些表现作出解释；但实际上，我们并不知道，与之同时发生的内在体验是不是在追兔子。

sentences.en: Another non-human dreamer offers insight here.
sentences.zh: 另一种会做梦的动物也为这个问题提供了线索。

sentences.en: In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room.
sentences.zh: 2019年，美国阿拉斯加太平洋大学的戴维·谢尔拍摄纪录片时，将一只名叫海蒂的章鱼养在自家客厅的水箱中。

sentences.en: At one point, in the middle of the night, Heidi seemed to dream: her limbs and head moved, and her skin rapidly changed colour, as though she was pursuing a crab.
sentences.zh: 有一次在半夜里，海蒂似乎做起梦来：它的腕和头动了起来，皮肤迅速变色，仿佛正在追逐一只螃蟹。

sentences.en: Similarly, a report recently emerged of a sleeping octopus apparently having a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 类似的是，最近有报道称，一只睡着的章鱼似乎在做噩梦。

sentences.en: Costello, as the octopus was called, thrashed around, extended his mantle as if trying to make himself look bigger, and squirted ink as though he were being attacked by a predator.
sentences.zh: 那只章鱼叫科斯特洛。它猛烈地扭动身体，伸展外套膜，像是想让自己显得更大；它还喷出墨汁，仿佛遭到了捕食者的袭击。

sentences.en: The nightmare study is intriguing, says Scheel, but is only based on one animal.
sentences.zh: 谢尔说，这项关于噩梦的研究很有意思，不过依据的只有一只动物的表现。

sentences.en: He argues that as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed to show that the octopuses are replaying sequences of activities from their waking lives in dreams.
sentences.zh: 他认为，除了观察外在行为，还得借助脑成像，才能证实章鱼在梦中按顺序重现了清醒时经历过的一连串活动。

sentences.en: The trouble is that we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们永远无法亲身体验任何动物的梦。

sentences.en: That goes for other humans' dreams too.
sentences.zh: 对于其他人的梦，道理也是一样的。

sentences.en: But we can try to imagine what these dreamscapes are like by meeting animals on their own terms.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍可以试着从动物自身的感知方式出发，去想象它们的梦境是什么样子。

sentences.en: For example, vision is the dominant sense for many humans, and so our dreams are heavily visual too.
sentences.zh: 比如，许多人的主导感官是视觉，所以他们的梦也有很强的视觉色彩。

sentences.en: Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.
sentences.zh: 狗主要靠嗅觉在周围环境中辨路，而蜘蛛在很大程度上靠的是振动。

sentences.en: It is likely that dreaming has served multiple purposes since the first complex animals evolved.
sentences.zh: 自从最早的复杂动物演化出现以来，做梦很可能就一直具有多种作用。

sentences.en: And if this is the case, it is possible that better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams.
sentences.zh: 如果确实如此，那么更好地理解这些作用，或许就能让我们认清人类自己做梦的真正用处。
